Client  
The Client application can be used to view Client information and Client Blacklist information 
and to manually blacklist a Client. 
Client Summary 
The Client Summary Screen provides a graphical view of the number of clients and system 
throughput on your network. The following viewing options are available by clicking on one of 
the drop-down lists at the top of the page: 
• 
View By - View information by AP/AP Group/Physical Map/Logical Map. Select "All" 
to view information for all APs. Select "APs", then select an AP to view information 
about a specific AP. Select "AP Group", then select an AP Group to view information 
about APs in a specific AP Group. Select "Physical Map", then select a physical map 
to view information about APs in a specific physical map. Select "Logical Map", then 
select a logical map to view information about APs in a specific logical map. 
• 
WLANs - View the information by WLAN. Select "All" to view information for all 
WLANs; or select a specific WLAN from the drop-down. Note that deleted WLANs 
(SSIDs) may still be displayed in the drop-down since the data retention period may 
still be valid. These deleted WLANs (SSIDs) will be indicated with an (*) next to the 
WLAN (SSID) name.

• 
Time Period - View information for a specific time period. Select "Fixed Period" to

Wireless Client List 
The Wireless Client List Screen displays real time information for wireless clients associated 
with APs. The Distribution of Clients per AP chart at the top of the screen provides a graphical 
overview of the number of clients associated with each AP. The All APs List provides 
information for each AP in the network. And the List of Clients on All APs provides information 
for all clients associated with an AP. It can also be used to manually "Blacklist" a client. 
All APs List 
• 
AP Name - Name of the AP. 
• 
Group Name - The AP Group to which the associated AP belongs. 
• 
AP MAC - The MAC address of the AP. 
• 
IP Address - The IP address of the AP. 
• 
IP Mode - The mode used to obtain the AP IP address (DHCP or Static). 
• 
Default Gateway - The default gateway used for AP forwarding. 
• 
Subnet Address - The IP subnet address of the AP. 
• 
AP Location - The AP location currently assigned in the AP. There are two location 
modes: 
LLDP Mode (Default) - The location is retrieved from the LLDP ALE TLV. 
Fixed/User String Mode - The location is hard coded with a user sting. 
• 
Status -The AP status: 
Up - AP is reachable. 
Down - AP is not reachable. 
Unknown - The AP has not been seen yet (AP was manually created/imported). 
• 
Registration Status - The registration status of the AP (e.g., Normal). 
• 
Country Code - The AP Country Code. 
• 
Management VLAN ID - The VLAN used to manage the AP. 
• 
AP Model - The model type of the AP (e.g., OAW-AP1221, OAW-AP1251). 
• 
AP Version - The AP OS version. 
• 
RF Profile - The RF Profile applied to the AP. 
• 
Client Count - The number of clients currently connected to the AP. 
• 
Neighbor AP - The neighbor AP to which the connected wireless client might roam. 
• 
Saved/Unsaved - Indicates whether or not the current AP configuration has been 
saved to OmniVista (Saved/Unsaved). 
• 
LED Model - The LED Mode configured for the AP. 
• 
DNS - The IP address of the DNS Server used by the AP. 
• 
Channel - The radio frequency working channel for the AP. 
• 
EIRP - The Effective Isotopically Radiated Power radio frequency for the AP. 
• 
LACP Status - Indicates whether or not the AP supports link aggregation 
(Supported/Unsupported). 
• 
Link Status - The LACP link status (Up/Down). 
• 
Work Mode - The AP Work Mode:

• 
AP Mode - AP serving wireless clients. 
• 
Mesh Mode - AP is working as a wireless mesh node.

List of Clients on All APs 
• 
Client Name - The name of the client. It is derived from the client’s system. 
• 
Group Name - The name of the AP Group to which the associated AP belongs. 
• 
AP MAC - The MAC address of the AP to which the client associated. 
• 
Associated SSID - The WLAN to which the client is associated. 
• 
MLO - Indicates whether the client is working in MultiLink Operation (MLO) mode 
(Yes/No). When the client is working in MLO mode (Yes), statistics are reported as

o The Channel, Attached Band, RSSI, and Working Mode are reported for the 
highest link that the client is using. 
o The connection rate (Rx and Tx) is reported as a total cummulative speed of 
all links. 
o The client detail page will display the 2.4G, 5G, and 6G link configration 
information. For example, if the client is working on 5G and 6G links, the detail 
page will include "5G Configuration" and "6G configuration" information.

Working Mode - The wireless working mode of the client.

Attached Band - The radio band through which the client attached to the AP

Client IP - The IP address of the client.

Device Category - The Client device type, including PC, Mobile, Tablet.

Device OS - The operating system of the client.

AP Name - The Name of AP to which the client associated. 
• 
Associate Time - The time when the client associated to the wireless network.

Channel - The working channel of the client. 
• 
RSSI - The Received Signal Strength Indicator of the client (Range = 0 - 99).

Rx Total - The total number of packets received by the client.

Rx Rate - The packet receive rate of the client.

Tx Rate - The packet sending rate of the client.

Access Role Profile - The Access Role Profile applied to the client after 
authentication.

VLAN - The VLAN through which the client accesses the network.

IP - The IP address of the far end tunnel termination.

Blacklisting a Client 
To blacklist a client, select the client(s) in the List of Clients on All APs and click on the Add to 
Blacklist button. Click OK at the Confirmation Prompt. The client will no longer be able to access 
the network and will be displayed on the Client Blacklist Screen. 
Wired Client List 
The Wired Client List Screen displays real time information for wired clients associated with 
APs. By default, all wired clients are displayed in the list. Click on the "Filter" link and select a 
criteria to filter the list of clients (e.g., Group Name, Client IP, Physical Map).

•

• 
Online Time - The length of time the client has been online. 
• 
Rx Bytes - The client receive traffic, in bytes. 
• 
Tx Bytes - The client transmit traffic, in bytes.

Map). You can also filter all sessions by date range by selecting "All" in the filter and setting a 
time range. The screen can also be used to show the roaming history of a client and its signal 
strength and export the Wireless Client Session List to a .csv file.

Show Roaming History for a Client 
To display roaming data for a client, select a client in the list and click on the Show Roaming 
and RSSI History button. A graphical history of the client's signal strength is displayed. By 
default, the past 24 Hours is displayed. Click on the Time Period field at the top of the screen to 
view data for the past 3 days. Use the slider at the bottom of the scree for a more detailed view 
of a specific time period. Click on the Show Client Session List button at the top of the screen 
to return to the original screen view.  
Note: To collect roaming data for a client, the following traps must be configured on 
APs: apStationAssociation and apStationDeassociation. Go to the Notifications 
application and configure the traps (Network - Notifications - Trap Configuration). See 
the Trap Configuration online help for more information. 
Exporting The Wireless Client Session List 
You can export the Wireless Client Session List to a CSV File. Click on the Export button and 
select All or Current.

Client Blocklist 
The Client Blocklist Screen displays information about all clients that have been blocklisted. It is 
also used to manually add clients to the Blocklist. 
Client Blocklist 
• 
Client MAC - MAC address of the client in the blocklist. 
• 
Start Date - The starting date for the blocklisting. During the duration, the client is 
not allowed to access to the wireless network. 
• 
Expiry Date - The expiration date for the blocklisting. The client can access the 
wireless network after the expiration date. 
• 
Reason - The reason why the client was added to blocklist. 
o Manually Add - Added into the Blocklist by the user.  
o Garbing Legal Accessing Client - Dynamically added by the WIPS policy. 
o Signal Strength is Too Strong, Reducing Network Performance - Dynamically 
added by the WIPS policy. 
o Channel Switching Too Often - Dynamically added by the WIPS policy. 
o Broadcasting Conflicted SSID, Misleading User Connection - Dynamically 
added by the WIPS policy. 
o Matching the Keyword of Suspected SSID - Dynamically added by the WIPS 
policy. 
o Matching the Suspected MAC OUI - Dynamically added by the WIPS policy. 
o Have Attacking Behavior - Dynamically added by the WIPS policy. 
o OmniVista secured your Network from a client connected to Access Point. 
Note: Quarantine Manager requires IoT to be enabled on Stellar APs through Network > 
Discovery > Managed Devices to detect and quarantine offending wireless clients that 
are connected to Stellar AP devices. The offending wireless client is not added to the 
Banned list; instead, the client is added to the Client Blocklist. See Using Quarantine 
Manager for Stellar AP Wireless Clients for more information.

Manually Adding a Client to the Blocklist 
Click on the Add icon to bring up the Add Client to Blocklist window. Enter the client's MAC 
address, then click on the Apply button. Repeat to add additional clients. 
Deleting a Client from the Blocklist 
Select the client(s) in the Blocklist and click on the Delete icon. Click OK at the confirmation 
prompt.
